correctness.rationale: For symmetric smooth densities, the nested Brownian-bridge increment formulas give the exact covariance and delta-method variance (RESULT.md Eq. (1)). The mixture ratio decreases strictly with its scale parameter (Eq. (2)), creating a unique continuous ratio-matching curve. certify.py computes exact rational bounds: variance >0.1915680 at weight 0.08 and variance <0.0277288 at 0.20, against Cauchy variance between 0.1022 and 0.1024. The intermediate-value theorem establishes an exact non-Cauchy mixture matching both center and variance; standard quantile CLT proves identical first-order Gaussian law. Explicit domain: iid samples, exact p=0.02217468, two-sided asymptotically Gaussian null calibration. Log output is supplementary; proof depends on displayed inequalities and source code.

originality.rationale: The primary four-quantile Cauchy paper (Pekgör, 2023) establishes the statistic and null law but its examined full text and alternatives table do not supply an exact two-Gaussian match of both population index and asymptotic variance. Rublík (2001) uses a fitted quadratic quantile statistic, not this fixed four-quantile ratio. Ebner, Eid, Klar (2022) use a Fourier–Stein statistic. A previously described Cauchy quantile-ratio result concerns fixed-sample extreme null tails and does not imply this non-Cauchy asymptotic power claim. Historical priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: The 2023 test explicitly chooses its outer quantiles for separation from a single Gaussian. Matching both the center and first-order null variance within an elementary two-normal, strictly unimodal, all-moments-finite alternative gives a consequential failure of consistency: Gaussian-calibrated rejection remains exactly nominal in the limit. This is stronger and more motivated than merely observing that a finite number of population quantiles cannot identify a distribution; it includes structural minimality and a certified nonlinear parameter crossing.
